Where things stand

As Figma stands, 215 colour pairs fail contrast; with the 77 fixes held in the repo, 0 do.

  • 533variables in the Figma snapshot: 308 semantic in 6 collections, 225 primitive in 4, each file with a checksum list (a8a60731, b51d9465)v2/figma/semantic.txt v2/figma/primitives.txt v2/figma/semantic.hashes.txt v2/figma/primitives.hashes.txt

  • 0colour pairs fail with the repo's fixes, of 682 scoredv2/report/data/contrast-merged.json
  • 77fixes held in the repo until Figma has them, each with its reasonds-tokens/overrides.json

The two directions and the merged one

Across 16 topics, V2 is stronger on 5, version 0.2 on 7 and both on 4; the merged direction keeps the stronger side of each.

TopicVersion 0.2V2 as givenStrongerMergedWhy
Token vocabulary68 semantic tokens with names of this repo's own: ground, panel, well, edge.308 semantic tokens in the product's own words: text, icon, surface, interactive, border, each with states, plus eleven accent hues, type roles, density and gradients.V2V2's names are the public names, unchanged. Engineers and designers already use them.A name nobody else uses is a private language. Version 0.2's names lose.
Where a name is writtenIn the repo's token file. Figma would be checked against code.In Figma, once. Everything else is generated.V2Figma owns names and values. The repo holds an exact snapshot, proved by checksum, and never edits it.Designers change values in Figma; a rule that sends them to a JSON file will be ignored.
What stops a bad value shippingA script fails the build on any contrast or naming breach, and each rule is proved on a planted fault.A contrast re-run by hand; failures listed as open items.Version 0.2Every snapshot passes through the contrast audit, the naming lint and the diff before it becomes CSS. A fix Figma does not hold yet lives in an overrides file with its reason, and the diff tool says when Figma has caught up.215 of 726 declared pairs fail in the Figma file today. A list of open items does not keep them out of the build.
ContrastEvery pair passes in light and dark; body text is held to 7 to 1.Brand text in dark 3.83, accent text in dark as low as 1.3, success and warning text in light about 3.2, placeholder 3.24, bold accent hover 3.32.Version 0.277 alias changes, each the nearest step on the same ramp, bring every declared pair to 4.5 (text) or 3 (icons, control edges, focus). 52 pairs are exempt and say why.WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor in the brief.
Edge of an inputA 3 to 1 edge token.border/primary at 1.35 to 1 against the page.Version 0.2border/primary stays a divider. A new border/strong at 3.05 to 1 or better is the edge of a control, as the naming standard's own example suggests.The edge is the only thing that shows where a field is.
Brand colourBlue, 108 degrees of hue or more from every status colour.Pink. In dark the primary fill (pink/600) and the destructive fill (red/600) have the same lightness and chroma and sit 27 degrees of hue apart.Version 0.2Pink stays: it is the owner's choice. The system stops relying on hue: links are underlined, errors carry an icon and words, a destructive button names its action, and a soft destructive variant differs from the primary in shape as well as colour.The brand is the owner's call; telling pink from red must not depend on colour vision.
Missing tokensBorder widths, focus ring, control sizes and durations exist as tokens.Border widths, motion and elevation are not started; no control height, icon size or scrim.Version 0.222 tokens proposed in the repo under the standard's naming rules, each with a reason, listed for adding to Figma.A button cannot be built from tokens without a height and a focus ring.
Text sizeNothing under 16 pixels.Body text 14, small 12, extra small 10.BothV2's scale stays: a dense work tool needs 14. A text field uses 16 where the pointer is a finger, because iOS zooms the page under 16. The 10 pixel roles are flagged for removal.Version 0.2 was sized for a checkout on a phone; the app is a work tool on a desktop as well.
Control size48 pixels everywhere, 56 for the main action.32 and 40 pixels.Both32, 40 and 44, and at least 44 wherever the pointer is a finger.40 is right for a mouse and small for a thumb.
ComponentsTen parts for a checkout and an assistant, in plain HTML and CSS, working with JavaScript off.Button, Input, Tabs, DropdownMenu, Dialog: the five the app uses most, in React on Radix.V2The five, in React on Radix, styled by a stylesheet that needs no framework. Version 0.2's ten stay on main, to re-point at the new tokens next.235 files in the app use Button. The first five must be the ones engineers reach for.
How a component is describedA Markdown note per part, with markup to copy.Two rules from Nathan Curtis: map states to data attributes, type every prop.V2A JSON spec per component against a schema: anatomy with roles, typed props with defaults, every state as a selector, token-only styles, and requirements that each name their check. The stylesheet, the typed props, the docs and the tests are generated from it.A note can say 'size: med' and nobody notices. A schema cannot.
Proof that a component does what its description saysA browser check of every screen at three widths and at 200 percent text; a checkout completed with scripts off.Storybook stories, to be written.Version 0.2A browser runner drives each component into each state the spec lists and compares the rendered colour with the token the spec names; runs axe; presses the keys; measures contrast, size and the focus ring.A story shows a state. It does not fail when the state is wrong.
Naming rulesA grammar enforced by a script.A written standard with ten rules, and a file that breaks several of them: radius named by height, type roles named small and base, typography prefixes that Tailwind will not pick up, no descriptions.BothThe owner's standard, enforced by a lint with 18 rules. The 24 places where the Figma file breaks its own standard are listed, not silently renamed.The standard is good. It needs a machine holding the file to it.
Versioning0.2.0 in this repo; an older 0.1.0 archived on a tag.Everything is v0.1.0 until 1.0.BothOne number for the whole system, as V2 says. Not 0.1.0 in this repo: that tag is already taken by the archived build. The standard's own table says a rename is a major change and an addition a minor one, which cannot hold if the number never moves.A version that never changes tells an engineer nothing.
FontThe system font: no download.Geist.V2Geist, self-hosted, shown with font-display swap so text is never blocked, with the system font behind it. It has no Japanese, Chinese or Korean glyphs; those fall back.The owner's choice, and a real typeface is part of a brand. The cost is one font file.
Unused weight144 tokens, all used.86 of 171 colour roles are used by no starred component; 63 gradient variables by none.Version 0.2Everything is generated for now: the whole token stylesheet is under 5 kilobytes compressed. The report lists every colour token no component uses.Removing the unnecessary is in the brief, but deleting a designer's tokens is not the lead's call.

From v2/report/comparison.json.

Why each pair must look different
  • primary-vs-destructive: The main action and the destructive action must not be mistaken for each other, including by people with red-green colour blindness.
  • brand-text-vs-error-text: Brand text and error text must not be mistaken for each other.
  • link-vs-error-text: A link and an error message must not be mistaken for each other.
  • brand-border-vs-error-border: A selected or branded field edge and an invalid field edge must look different.
  • focus-vs-info: A focus ring and an info border share a hue; note whether they are the same colour.
  • primary-hover-vs-default: Hover must be visibly different from rest.
  • primary-active-vs-hover: Pressed must be visibly different from hover.
  • surface-hover-vs-disabled: One job per token: a hovered surface and a disabled surface should not be the same grey.
  • surface-hover-vs-secondary: One job per token: a hovered primary surface and the resting secondary surface should not be the same grey.

Naming

The naming lint ran 18 rules over the Figma snapshot and found 66 findings: 24 break the written standard, 30 need a person to decide and 12 are notes.

Breaks the standard (24 findings, 511 names)

The file contradicts a written rule of the standard.

  • name-case: These names have a part that is not lowercase kebab-case (capital letters, spaces, a leading or trailing hyphen, or other characters). For example primitive Colors: neutral/dark/-100.
  • size-scale: These names use xsmall, small, base, medium or large instead of xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl. For example Typography: font-size/section-label-base (base -> md), Typography: font-size/label-large (large -> lg), and 20 more.
  • size-scale: These radius names are taken from a pixel value (the height of the thing they round), which the standard forbids. For example Radius: height/16, Radius: height/20, and 6 more.

Decide (30 findings, 627 names)

A person has to choose.

  • state-set: These surface or interactive groups have a hover state but no active or disabled state. Either the set is incomplete or these groups are meant to have only hover. For example Themes: interactive/error/* (lacks active and disabled), Themes: interactive/success/* (lacks active and disabled), and 31 more.
  • state-set: Sibling groups are written differently: one has states, the other is a single token without /default. For example Themes: border/secondary has no states while border/primary/* has them.
  • size-scale: These semantic names are numbers (the pixel value times ten), not the xs to 2xl scale. The standard names radius/height/20 as the example; it does not say whether a spacing step counts. For example Density: scaled/400, Density: scaled/320, and 24 more.

Note (12 findings, 51 names)

Listed for a person to confirm.

  • alias: These aliases cross modes (a dark value points at a light neutral, or the other way) where their siblings do not. Listed, not failed: it may be intended. For example Themes: text/on (dark -> neutral/light/0), Themes: icon/on (dark -> neutral/light/0), and 2 more.
  • same-in-both-modes: 37 colour tokens have the same value in light and dark. Confirm each is meant. For example Themes: text/on (#ffffff), Themes: icon/on (#ffffff), and 35 more.
  • missing-categories: Not started: no variable name or collection covers border width. For example category: border width.

What is not proven

29 things on this page are not proven, including 18 requirements only a person can check and 0 inputs that are missing or unreadable.

  • Button: While loading, the label says what is happening, such as Saving, and keeps any amount. (button-loading-label, checked by hand only)
  • Button: A danger button states the destructive action in its label, such as Delete project, because in the dark theme its fill is close in colour to the primary fill. (button-error-not-colour-alone, checked by hand only)
  • Dialog: A confirmation of an action that cannot be undone, such as deleting or paying, uses AlertDialog rather than Dialog. (dialog-not-destructive, checked by hand only)
  • Dialog: A dialog does not open another dialog. A second step replaces the body of the first. (dialog-no-nesting, checked by hand only)
  • Dialog: On a phone, a task longer than one screen of body moves to its own page instead of a dialog, because a scrolling body inside a window is harder to read than a page. (dialog-short-task, checked by hand only)
  • DropdownMenu: An item with variant danger names what it destroys in its label, such as Delete chat, because red alone does not tell everyone that the action is destructive. (dropdown-menu-danger-not-colour-alone, checked by hand only)
  • DropdownMenu: A choice of one from several uses a radio group, an independent on or off setting uses a checkbox item, and only commands use plain items, so the checked state is announced. (dropdown-menu-right-item-kind, checked by hand only)
  • DropdownMenu: The trigger's chevron icon points up while the menu is open and down while it is closed, chosen from aria-expanded, as the model selector fixes ask. People may read the flipped chevron as a sign the menu can be closed again. (dropdown-menu-trigger-shows-open, checked by hand only)
  • DropdownMenu: A group holds about seven items or fewer, on the belief that people scan a short menu faster than a long one; a longer list of choices belongs in a list or a dialog. (dropdown-menu-short-groups, checked by hand only)
  • DropdownMenu: A checkbox item could keep the menu open when chosen, by calling preventDefault in onSelect, so several settings can be changed in one visit. Whether people expect this in Souvenir's menus is untested. (dropdown-menu-checkbox-stays-open, checked by hand only)
  • Input: The placeholder is never the only label or the only instruction; it disappears as soon as the person types. (input-placeholder-not-label, checked by hand only)
  • Input: Amounts, card numbers, postal codes and one-time codes use type text with inputMode numeric or decimal, not type number, which changes the value on scroll, drops leading zeros and is read poorly by some screen readers. (input-no-number-for-codes, checked by hand only)
  • Input: The error message says what is wrong and how to fix it, such as Enter an email address, such as name@example.com. (input-error-says-fix, checked by hand only)
  • Input: The product shows an error when the person leaves the field or submits, not while they are still typing, and removes it as soon as the value is fixed. (input-validate-on-leave, checked by hand only)
  • Input: People understand the word Required next to a label faster than an asterisk explained elsewhere on the page. (input-required-word-understood, checked by hand only)
  • Tabs: Use activationMode manual when a panel's content is fetched or slow to show, so that moving focus along the list does not load every panel on the way. (tabs-manual-for-slow-panels, checked by hand only)
  • Tabs: Tabs show views of the same thing that can be visited in any order. They are not used for the steps of a sequence such as checkout. (tabs-not-for-steps, checked by hand only)
  • Tabs: On a phone, keep to the number of tabs that fit without scrolling, about two to four, so no tab is hidden off screen. (tabs-few-tabs, checked by hand only)
